unitemized.reason: A frontend accessibility standard that only applies when UI markup is written. Proper heading order in UI code is a subjective code-quality matter that no deterministic kind can check, and the 'frontend change' condition can't be written as a predicate.
A SHOULD-style CSS preference that only applies when styles are written. Whether rem/em were preferred over px is a judgment call with no observable predicate.
Only applies when there are UI changes, which can't be written as an applies_when predicate. Testing across mobile, tablet and desktop leaves no evidence that exec_evidence can recognize.
A UI design guideline about tap target size. It only applies to UI code and can't be checked deterministically from the trace or the diff.
A general code-style guideline (consistent formatting). It is subjective and no kind in the vocabulary can check it.
A naming-quality guideline with a fuzzy exception ('except in narrow contexts'). It can't be checked deterministically.
A style guideline about consistent indentation. No kind checks code formatting, and the rule is too weak to justify an unimplemented item.
Setting up an editor or linter is advice, not a required step of the workflow. Whether it applies depends on the repo, which no predicate can express.
An error-handling design preference (specific rather than generic exceptions). It is a subjective code-quality judgment that no kind can check.
